questions.q: Which prefix makes the opposite of *legal*?
questions.explain: *il-* is used before *l*: *illegal*.

questions.q: Which word is a compound adjective?
questions.explain: *well-known* joins two words into one adjective; hyphenate it before a noun.

questions.q: It's a *___* walk to the station.
questions.explain: In a compound adjective before a noun, the noun stays singular: *a ten-minute walk*.

questions.q: *___* I need is a long holiday.
questions.explain: A *wh*-cleft: *What I need is…* focuses on *a long holiday*.

questions.q: *___* was my sister who told me the news.
questions.explain: An *it*-cleft: *It was … who/that …* puts focus on one element.

questions.q: Never *___* such a beautiful sunset.
questions.explain: After a negative adverb at the front, the auxiliary comes before the subject (inversion).

questions.q: No sooner had we sat down *___* the phone rang.
questions.explain: *no sooner … than*; *hardly / scarcely … when*.

questions.q: She is not only clever *___* very kind.
questions.explain: The pair is *not only … but (also)*.

questions.q: *___* the rain, the match continued.
questions.explain: *despite* + noun; *although / even though* need a clause.

questions.q: *___* it was late, we decided to walk home.
questions.explain: *although* + clause expresses contrast.

questions.q: I'll lend you the car *___* you drive carefully.
questions.explain: *as long as* = only if, on condition that.

questions.q: We'll go for a walk *___* it rains.
questions.explain: *unless* = if not: we'll go if it doesn't rain.

questions.q: I've known her *___* we were at school together.
questions.explain: *since* + a point in time or a clause, with the present perfect.

questions.q: I'm not sure *___* to accept the offer.
questions.explain: Before a *to*-infinitive, use *whether*, not *if*.

questions.q: *___* a beautiful day!
questions.explain: *What (a) + noun* in exclamations; *How + adjective*.

questions.q: *___* many people at the concert.
questions.explain: *there + be* introduces the existence of something; the verb agrees with *people*.

questions.q: The list of names *___* very long.
questions.explain: The verb agrees with the head noun *list*, not with *names*.

questions.q: My brother, *___* lives in Rome, is a chef.
questions.explain: Non-defining relative clauses use *who* or *which*, never *that*.

questions.q: He forgot my birthday, *___* really upset me.
questions.explain: *which* refers back to a whole clause.

questions.q: That's the girl *___* father is a pilot.
questions.explain: *whose* shows possession in relative clauses.

questions.q: I *___* she'll come.
questions.explain: With *think*, we usually make the main verb negative: *I don't think she'll come*.

questions.q: I can *___* hear you.
questions.explain: *hardly* is already negative; don't add *not*.

questions.q: "I don't like spiders." "*___*"
questions.explain: To agree with a negative statement: *Neither / Nor do I* (or *Me neither*).

questions.q: *___* called you last night?
questions.explain: When *who* is the subject, there is no *do / did*: *Who called you?*

questions.q: Can you tell me where *___*?
questions.explain: Indirect questions use statement word order.
